subject: English
passage: In the early 1900s, Italian-language theaters flourished in neighborhoods across New York City. Brooklyn alone hosted fifteen Italian theaters between 1905 and 1915. But Manhattan exceeded all other boroughs in the city. This borough hosted twenty-eight Italian theaters during that period. Manhattan had the largest concentration of recent Italian immigrants and established Little Italy as a cultural hub. Thus, it is understandable that this borough became such a vibrant center for Italian theatrical productions.
prompt: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?

choices.A: To contrast Italian-language theaters that operated in New York City with ones that operated there during the early 1900s
choices.B: To argue that Italian-language theaters established in Manhattan shaped the ones established in Brooklyn during the early 1900s
choices.C: To explain why Italian-language theaters operating in New York City were so influential in Italy during the early 1900s
choices.D: To explain that Italian-language theaters prospered in New York City and particularly in Manhattan during the early 1900s

explanation:
Choice D is the best answer because it most accurately describes the main purpose of the text. The text begins by stating that there were many Italian-language theaters in neighborhoods across New York City in the early 1900s, citing Brooklyn as a borough that hosted fifteen such theaters. The text then goes on to note that in Manhattan, there were twenty-eight Italian theaters in the early 1900s, more than any other borough. The text then concludes by explaining that the reason for this large number of Italian theaters was likely Manhattan's concentration of Italian immigrants and its role as a cultural hub. Therefore, the main purpose of the text is to explain that Italian-language theaters prospered in New York City, particularly in Manhattan, in the early 1900s.

Why B is incorrect:

Choice B is incorrect. Although the text characterizes Manhattan as a vibrant center for Italian theatrical productions in the early 1900s, the text doesn't discuss whether theaters established in Manhattan shaped the theaters established in other boroughs, including Brooklyn.
